# The 82 solved puzzle keys + how to construct more (v1, 2026-07-14)

Self-contained dataset for detector testing: every solved key with its public
(address, X, Y), private (`d`), and the exact `(n, k, derr, D)` decomposition —
plus a recipe (`construct_key`) to make **new** solved keys of **any** construction
so any detector can be validated on known answers before it is aimed at unknowns.

Regenerate / integrity-check: `emit_solved_keys_dataset_v1.py` (writes
`solved_keys_augmented_v1.csv`; **82/82** keys reproduce their on-chain `X,Y` via
exact `scalar_mul`). Source rows: `puzzles_verified.csv`.

## Field definitions (all exact integers)

For a key of size `bits` with private scalar `d`:
- `A = 2^(bits-1)` — band base;  `band_offset = d − A`.
- `(X, Y) = [d]G` — the public point (`ecc_secp256k1.scalar_mul`, exact Jacobian).
- `(n, k) = best_nk(d, bits)` — Farey best rational of `band_offset / A` over
  denominators `n ≤ 256`: `argmin_{n≤256, 0≤k≤n} |n·(d−A) − k·A|`, then reduced by `gcd`.
- `derr = |n·(d−A) − k·A|` — the exact residual of that `(n,k)` approximation.
- `D_terms = d_recursion(2^bits, d)` — greedy nearest-unit-fraction (Engel-like)
  expansion; an **invertible** encoding of `d` (reproduces the dataset `D_terms`
  column 40260/40260, per `d_recursion_exact_v1`). `n_Dterms = len(D_terms)`.

Note two distinct "D"s in the corpus: **this** `D_terms` (the invertible
d-signature) and the curve-identity scalar `D` in `n·Q−(n+k)·A=r·G,
r=n·D−(2^{N−1}·k mod n)` (`btc_puzzle_exact_leak_test`). They are different objects;
this file uses `D_terms`.

## How to construct MORE solved keys (any construction)

```python
from emit_solved_keys_dataset_v1 import construct_key
# any d you like, by any rule -> full known-answer record (verified on-curve):
rec = construct_key(d, bits)      # {d, X, Y, n, k, derr, D_terms, band_offset, ...}
```
`construct_key(d, bits)` computes `[d]G` and the full `(n,k,derr,D)` decomposition
for **any** chosen `d`. Pick `d` by whatever construction you want to test a
detector against — examples (`example_constructions`, 64-bit):

| construction | d | n | k | derr | #D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| random-in-band | `A + rand(A)` | 61 | 47 | 667981189358631 | 6 |
| sum-of-fractions `N/3+N/7` | (Finding B) | 1 | 0 | 439208192231179801 | 4 |
| `N/3+N/7+N/13+2^(b/8)` | (Finding C) | 160 | 17 | 33785245556203776 | 6 |
| low-band-offset | `A + 12345` | 1 | 0 | 12345 | 3 |
| near-top | `N − 999` | 1 | 1 | 999 | 2 |

The 100k MT19937 reference set is exactly this pipeline driven by our MT19937
(select bit-length → random-in-band `d` → curve); the constructed set is therefore a
**full-power known-generator** reference — test every detector on both it and the
real 82 (memory `feedback_test_on_both_sets`).
